paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 26 to 35 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 26 至 35 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Surfing the Internet during class doesn't just steal focus from the educator; it also hurts students who're already struggling to 26 the material. A new study from Michigan State University, though, argues that all students—including high achievers—see a decline in performance when they browse the Internet during class for non-academic purposes.

To measure the effects of Internet-based distractions during class, researchers 27 500 students taking an introductory psychology class at Michigan State University. Researchers used ACT scores as a measure of intellectual

28 . Because previous research has shown that people with high intellectual abilities are better at 29 out distractions, researchers believed students with high ACT scores would not show a 30 decrease in performance due to their use of digital devices. But students who surfed the web during class did worse on their exams regardless of their ACT scores, suggesting that even the academically smartest students are harmed when they're distracted in class.

College professors are increasingly 31 alarm bells about the effects smartphones, laptops, and tablets have on academic performance. One 2013 study of college students found that 80% of students use their phones or laptops during class, with the average student checking their digital device 11 times in a 32 class. A quarter of students report that their use of digital devices during class causes their grades to 33 .

Professors sometimes implement policies designed to 34 students' use of digital devices, and some instructors even confiscate (没收) tablets and phones. In a world where people are increasingly dependent on their phones, though, such strategies often fail. One international study found that 84% of people say they couldn't go a day without their smartphones. Until students are able to 35 the pull of social networking, texting, and endlessly surfing the web, they may continue to struggle in their classes.

Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: A Pioneering Woman of Science Re-Emerges after 300 Years
paragraphs.translationZh: 一位科学先锋女性在 300 年后重新崛起

paragraphs.sourceText: A. Maria Sibylla Merian, like many European women of the 17th century, stayed busy managing a household and rearing children. But on top of that, Merian, a German-born woman who lived in the Netherlands, also managed a successful career as an artist, botanist, naturalist and entomologist （昆虫学家）.
paragraphs.translationZh: A. 玛丽亚·西比拉·梅里安 (A. Maria Sibylla Merian) 和许多 17 世纪的欧洲女性一样，一直忙于管理家庭和抚养孩子。但最重要的是，梅里安，一位出生于德国、居住在荷兰的女性，作为一名艺术家、植物学家、博物学家和昆虫学家，也取得了成功的职业生涯。

paragraphs.sourceText: B. “She was a scientist on the level with a lot of people we spend a lot of time talking about,” said Kay Etheridge, a biologist at Gettysburg College in Pennsylvania who has been studying the scientific history of Merian’s work. “She didn't do as much to change biology as Charles Darwin, but she was significant.”
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 宾夕法尼亚州葛底斯堡学院的生物学家凯·埃瑟里奇（Kay Etheridge）一直在研究梅里安工作的科学史，他说：“她是一位与我们花了很多时间谈论的很多人一样水平的科学家。” “她在改变生物学方面的贡献不如查尔斯·达尔文那么多，但她的意义重大。”

paragraphs.sourceText: C. At a time when natural history was a valuable tool for discovery, Merian discovered facts about plants and insects that were not previously known. Her observations helped dismiss the popular belief that insects spontaneously emerged from mud. The knowledge she collected over decades didn't just satisfy those curious about nature, but also provided valuable insights into medicine and science. She was the first to bring together insects and their habitats, including food they ate, into a single ecological composition.
paragraphs.translationZh: C. 在自然历史成为发现的宝贵工具的时代，梅里安发现了以前不为人知的有关植物和昆虫的事实。她的观察结果驳斥了人们普遍认为昆虫是从泥土中自然出现的观点。她几十年来收集的知识不仅满足了人们对自然的好奇，还为医学和科学提供了宝贵的见解。她是第一个将昆虫及其栖息地（包括它们所吃的食物）整合为单一生态组合的人。

paragraphs.sourceText: D. After years of pleasing a fascinated audience across Europe with books of detailed descriptions and life-size paintings of familiar insects, in 1699 she sailed with her daughter nearly 5,000 miles from the Netherlands to South America to study insects in the jungles of what is now known as Suriname. She was 52 years old. The result was her masterpiece, Metamorphosis Insectorum Surinamensium.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 多年来，她用详细描述的书籍和对常见昆虫的真人大小的绘画取悦了欧洲各地的着迷的观众，1699 年，她与女儿从荷兰航行近 5,000 英里到达南美洲，研究现在称为苏里南的丛林中的昆虫。她52岁了。结果就是她的杰作《Metamorphosis Insectorum Surinamensium》。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. In her work, she revealed a side of nature so exotic, dramatic and valuable to Europeans of the time that she received much acclaim. But a century later, her findings came under scientific criticism. Shoddy（粗糙的）reproductions of her work along with setbacks to women's roles in 18th- and 19th-century Europe resulted in her efforts being largely forgotten. “It was kind of stunning when she sort of dropped off into oblivion （遗忘）,” said Dr. Etheridge. “Victorians started putting women in a box, and they're still trying to crawl out of it.”
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 在她的作品中，她向当时的欧洲人展示了自然的一面，充满异国情调、戏剧性和有价值，因此受到了广泛的赞誉。但一个世纪后，她的发现受到了科学批评。她的作品的粗制滥造以及 18 世纪和 19 世纪欧洲女性角色的挫折导致她的努力基本上被遗忘。 “当她渐渐被遗忘时，这真是令人震惊，”埃瑟里奇博士说。 “维多利亚时代的人开始把女性关在盒子里，而她们仍然试图从里面爬出来。”

paragraphs.sourceText: F. Today, the pioneering woman of the sciences has re-emerged. In recent years, feminists, historians and artists have all praised Merian's tenacity （坚韧）, talent and inspirational artistic compositions. And now biologists like Dr. Etheridge are digging into the scientific texts that accompanied her art. Three hundred years after her death, Merian will be celebrated at an international symposium in Amsterdam this June.
paragraphs.translationZh: F. 今天，这位科学界的先驱女性重新出现。近年来，女权主义者、历史学家和艺术家都称赞梅里安的坚韧、才华和鼓舞人心的艺术作品。现在，像埃瑟里奇博士这样的生物学家正在深入研究伴随她的艺术的科学文本。梅里安去世三百年后，将于今年六月在阿姆斯特丹举行的国际研讨会上进行庆祝。

paragraphs.sourceText: G. And last month, Metamorphosis Insectorum Surinamensium was republished. It contains 60 plates （插图）and original descriptions, along with stories about Merian's life and updated scientific descriptions. Before writing Metamorphosis, Merian spent decades documenting European plants and insects that she published in a series of books. She began in her 20s, making textless, decorative paintings of flowers with insects. “Then she got really serious,” Dr. Etheridge said. Merian started raising insects at home, mostly butterflies and caterpillars. “She would sit up all night until they came out of the pupa （蛹）so she could draw them,” she said.
paragraphs.translationZh: G. 上个月，《Metamorphosis Insectorum Surinamensium》重新出版。它包含 60 个插图（插图）和原始描述，以及有关梅里安生活的故事和更新的科学描述。在写《变形记》之前，梅里安花了几十年时间记录欧洲植物和昆虫，并出版了一系列书籍。她从 20 多岁开始创作无文字的花卉和昆虫装饰画。 “然后她变得非常严肃，”埃瑟里奇博士说。梅里安开始在家饲养昆虫，主要是蝴蝶和毛毛虫。 “她会整夜坐着，直到它们从蛹中出来，这样她就可以画它们，”她说。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. The results of her decades' worth of careful observations were detailed paintings and descriptions of European insects, followed by unconventional visuals and stories of insects and animals from a land that most at the time could only imagine. It's possible Merian used a magnifying glass to capture the detail of the split tongues of sphinx moths （斯芬克斯飞蛾）depicted in the painting. She wrote that the two tongues combine to form one tube for drinking nectar （花蜜）. Some criticized this detail later, saying there was just one tongue, but Merian wasn't wrong. She may have observed the adult moth just as it emerged from its pupa. For a brief moment during that stage of its life cycle, the tongue consists of two tiny half-tubes before merging into one.
paragraphs.translationZh: H. 她几十年来仔细观察的结果是对欧洲昆虫的详细绘画和描述，随后是来自这片当时大多数人只能想象的土地上的昆虫和动物的非传统视觉效果和故事。梅里安可能使用放大镜捕捉到画中描绘的斯芬克斯飞蛾分裂舌头的细节。她写道，两只舌头合在一起形成一根管子，用来喝花蜜。后来有人批评这个细节，说只有一个舌头，但梅里安并没有错。她可能观察到了成蛾刚从蛹中出来时的情况。在其生命周期的这一阶段的短暂时刻，舌头由两个微小的半管组成，然后合并成一个。

paragraphs.sourceText: I. It may not have been ladylike to depict a giant spider devouring a hummingbird, but when Merian did it at the turn of the 18th century, surprisingly, nobody objected. Dr. Etheridge called it revolutionary. The image, which also contained novel descriptions of ants, fascinated a European audience that was more concerned with the exotic story unfolding before them than the gender of the person who painted it.
paragraphs.translationZh: I. 描绘一只巨大的蜘蛛吞噬一只蜂鸟可能不太淑女，但当梅里安在 18 世纪之交这样做时，令人惊讶的是，没有人反对。埃瑟里奇博士称其为革命性的。这幅图像还包含对蚂蚁的新颖描述，令欧洲观众着迷，他们更关心眼前展开的异国故事，而不是画者的性别。

paragraphs.sourceText: J. “All of these things shook up their nice, neat little view,” Dr. Etheridge said. But later, people of the Victorian era thought differently. Her work had been reproduced, sometimes incorrectly. A few observations were deemed impossible. “She'd been called a silly woman for saying that a spider could eat a bird,” Dr. Etheridge said. But Henry Walter Bates, a friend of Charles Darwin, observed it and put it in book in 1863, proving Merian was correct.
paragraphs.translationZh: J.“所有这些东西都震撼了他们美丽、整洁的小视野，”埃瑟里奇博士说。但后来，维多利亚时代的人们却有了不同的想法。她的作品被复制，有时是错误的。一些观察被认为是不可能的。 “她因为说蜘蛛可以吃鸟而被称为傻女人，”埃瑟里奇博士说。但查尔斯·达尔文 (Charles Darwin) 的朋友亨利·沃尔特·贝茨 (Henry Walter Bates) 观察到了这一现象，并于 1863 年将其记入书中，证明了梅里安的正确性。

paragraphs.sourceText: K. In the same plate, Merian depicted and described leaf-cutter ants for the first time. “In America there are large ants which can eat whole trees bare as a broom handle in a single night,” she wrote in the description. Merian noted how the ants took the leaves below ground to their young. And she wouldn't have known this at the time, but the ants use the leaves to farm fungi （菌类）underground to feed their developing babies.
paragraphs.translationZh: K. 在同一版中，梅里安首次描绘和描述了切叶蚁。她在描述中写道：“在美国，有一种大型蚂蚁，它们可以在一夜之间把整棵树吃得像扫帚柄一样光秃秃的。”梅里安记录了蚂蚁如何将地下的叶子带给它们的幼崽。她当时并不知道，蚂蚁利用叶子在地下种植真菌来喂养正在发育的婴儿。

paragraphs.sourceText: L. Merian was correct about the giant bird-eating spiders, ants building bridges with their bodies and other details. But in the same drawing, she incorrectly lumped together army and leaf-cutter ants. And instead of showing just the typical pair of eggs in a hummingbird nest, she painted four. She made other mistakes in Metamorphosis Insectorum Surinamensium as well: not every caterpillar and butterfly matched.
paragraphs.translationZh: L. Merian 关于巨型食鸟蜘蛛、蚂蚁用身体搭建桥梁以及其他细节的说法是正确的。但在同一张图中，她错误地将军蚁和切叶蚁混为一谈。她没有只展示蜂鸟巢中典型的一对蛋，而是画了四个。她在《苏里南昆虫变形记》中还犯了其他错误：并非所有毛毛虫和蝴蝶都匹配。

paragraphs.sourceText: M. Perhaps one explanation for her mistakes is that she cut short her Suriname trip after getting sick, and completed the book at home in Amsterdam. And errors are common among some of history's most-celebrated scientific minds, too. “These errors no more invalidate Ms. Merian's work than do well-known misconceptions published by Charles Darwin or Isaac Newton,” Dr. Etheridge wrote in a paper that argued that too many have wrongly focused on the mistakes of her work.
paragraphs.translationZh: M：也许对她的错误的一个解释是，她在生病后缩短了苏里南之旅，并在阿姆斯特丹的家中完成了这本书。在历史上一些最著名的科学思想家中，错误也很常见。埃瑟里奇博士在一篇论文中写道：“这些错误并不比查尔斯·达尔文或艾萨克·牛顿发表的众所周知的误解更能证明梅里安女士的工作无效。”该论文认为，太多人错误地关注了她工作中的错误。

paragraphs.sourceText: N. Merian’s paintings inspired artists and ecologists. In an 1801 drawing from his book, General Zoology Amphibia, George Shaw, an English botanist and zoologist, credited Merian for describing a frog in the account of her South American expedition, and named the young tree frog after her in his portrayal of it. It wouldn't be fair to give Merian all the credit. She received assistance naming plants, making sketches and referencing the work of others. Her daughters helped her color her drawings.
paragraphs.translationZh: N. Merian 的画作给艺术家和生态学家带来了灵感。英国植物学家和动物学家乔治·肖 (George Shaw) 在 1801 年的《两栖动物学概论》一书中绘制了一幅图画，称赞梅里安在她的南美探险记中描述了一只青蛙，并在描述中以她的名字为这只小树蛙命名。将所有功劳都归于梅里安是不公平的。她在命名植物、绘制草图和参考他人作品方面得到了帮助。她的女儿们帮她给画作上色。

paragraphs.sourceText: O. Merian also made note of the help she received from the natives of Suriname, as well as slaves or servants that assisted her. In some instances she wrote moving passages that included her helpers in descriptions. As she wrote in her description of the peacock flower, “The Indians, who are not treated well by their Dutch masters, use the seeds to abort their children, so that they will not become slaves like themselves. The black slaves from Guinea and Angola have demanded to be well treated, threatening to refuse to have children. In fact, they sometimes take their own lives because they are treated so badly, and because they believe they will be born again, free and living in their own land. They told me this themselves.” [P] Londa Schiebinger, a professor of the history of science at Stanford University, called this passage rather astonishing. It's particularly striking centuries later when these issues are still prominent in public discussions about social justice and women’s rights. “She was ahead of her time,” Dr. Etheridge said.
paragraphs.translationZh: 奥·梅里安还记录了她从苏里南当地人以及帮助她的奴隶或仆人那里得到的帮助。在某些情况下，她写了感人的段落，其中描述了她的助手。正如她在描述孔雀花时所写的那样，“受到荷兰主人待遇不佳的印第安人，用孔雀花的种子堕胎，这样他们就不会像自己一样成为奴隶。几内亚和安哥拉的黑奴要求得到良好的对待，并威胁拒绝生孩子。事实上，他们有时会结束自己的生命，因为他们受到如此恶劣的待遇，因为他们相信自己会重生，自由地生活在自己的土地上。这些都是他们自己告诉我的。” [P] 斯坦福大学科学史教授隆达·希宾格 (Londa Schiebinger) 称这段话相当令人惊讶。几个世纪后，当这些问题在有关社会正义和妇女权利的公共讨论中仍然突出时，这一点尤其引人注目。 “她领先于她的时代，”埃瑟里奇博士说。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Merian was the first scientist to study a type of American ant.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 梅里安是第一位研究美洲蚂蚁的科学家。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. The European audience was more interested in Merian's drawings than her gender.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 欧洲观众对梅里安的画作比她的性别更感兴趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38.Merian's masterpiece came under attack a century after its publication.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38.梅里安的杰作在出版一个世纪后就受到攻击。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Merian’s mistakes in her drawings may be attributed to her shortened stay in South America.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 梅里安在绘画中的错误可能归因于她在南美停留的时间较短。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Merian often sat up the whole night through to observe and draw insects.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 梅里安经常整夜坐着观察和画昆虫。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Merian acknowledged the help she got from natives of South America.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 梅里安感谢她从南美洲当地人那里得到的帮助。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Merian contributed greatly to people's better understanding of medicine and science.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 梅里安为人们更好地理解医学和科学做出了巨大贡献。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Merian occasionally made mistakes in her drawings of insects and birds.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 梅里安在画昆虫和鸟类时偶尔会犯错误。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Now, Merian's role as a female forerunner in sciences has been re-established.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 现在，梅里安作为科学领域女性先驱的角色已经重新确立。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45.Merian made a long voyage to South America to study jungle insects over three centuries ago.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45.三个多世纪前，梅里安长途跋涉前往南美洲研究丛林昆虫。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: While human achievements in mathematics continue to reach new levels of complexity, many of us who aren't mathematicians at heart (or engineers by trade) may struggle to remember the last time we used calculus (微积分).
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然人类在数学方面的成就不断达到新的复杂水平，但我们中的许多人本质上不是数学家（或工程师）可能很难记住上次使用微积分（微积分）是什么时候。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s a fact not lost on American educators, who amid rising math failure rates are debating how math can better meet the real-life needs of students. Should we change the way math is taught in schools, or eliminate some courses entirely?
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国教育工作者并没有忽视这一事实，在数学不及格率不断上升的情况下，他们正在讨论数学如何更好地满足学生的现实生活需求。我们应该改变学校数学教学的方式，还是完全取消一些课程？

paragraphs.sourceText: Andrew Hacker, Queens College political science professor, thinks that advanced algebra and other higher-level math should be cut from curricula in favor of courses with more routine usefulness, like statistics.
paragraphs.translationZh: 皇后学院政治学教授安德鲁·哈克（Andrew Hacker）认为，高等代数和其他高级数学应该从课程中删除，转而开设具有更多常规用途的课程，例如统计学。

paragraphs.sourceText: “We hear on all sides that we're not teaching enough mathematics, and the Chinese are running rings around us,” Hacker says. “I'm suggesting we're teaching too much mathematics to too many people…not everybody has to know calculus. If you're going to become an aeronautical (航空的) engineer, fine. But most of us aren't.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “我们从各个方面都听说我们没有教授足够的数学，而中国人在我们周围跑来跑去，”哈克说。 “我建议我们向太多人教授太多数学……并不是每个人都必须了解微积分。如果你想成为一名航空工程师，那很好。但我们大多数人都不是。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Instead, Hacker is pushing for more courses like the one he teaches at Queens College：Numeracy 101. There, his students of “citizen statistics” learn to analyze public information like the federal budget and corporate reports. Such courses, Hacker argues, are a remedy for the numerical illiteracy of adults who have completed high-level math like algebra but are unable to calculate the price of, say, a carpet by area.
paragraphs.translationZh: 相反，哈克正在推动更多的课程，比如他在皇后学院教授的课程：计算101。在那里，他的“公民统计”学生学习分析联邦预算和公司报告等公共信息。哈克认为，此类课程可以弥补成年人的数字文盲，他们已经完成了代数等高级数学课程，但无法计算（例如按面积计算地毯）的价格。

paragraphs.sourceText: Hacker's argument has met with opposition from other math educators who say what's needed is to help students develop a better relationship with math earlier, rather than teaching them less math altogether.
paragraphs.translationZh: 哈克的论点遭到了其他数学教育工作者的反对，他们认为需要的是帮助学生更早地与数学建立更好的关系，而不是完全教他们更少的数学。

paragraphs.sourceText: Maria Droujkova is a founder of Natural Math, and has taught basic calculus concepts to 5-year-olds. For Droujkova, high-level math is important, and what it could use in American classrooms is an injection of childlike wonder.
paragraphs.translationZh: Maria Droujkova 是 Natural Math 的创始人，向 5 岁的孩子教授基本的微积分概念。对于德鲁伊科娃来说，高级数学很重要，它在美国课堂上的作用是注入童趣的好奇心。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Make mathematics more available,” Droujkova says. “Redesign it so it's more accessible to more kinds of people: young children, adults who worry about it, adults who may have had bad experiences.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “让数学变得更加可用，”德鲁伊科娃说。 “重新设计它，使其更容易被更多类型的人使用：幼儿、担心它的成年人、可能有过不良经历的成年人。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Pamela Harris, a lecturer at the University of Texas at Austin, has a similar perspective. Harris says that American education is suffering from an epidemic of “fake math”—an emphasis on rote memorization (死记硬背) of formulas and steps, rather than an understanding of how math can influence the ways we see the world.
paragraphs.translationZh: 德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校讲师帕梅拉·哈里斯也有类似的观点。哈里斯说，美国教育正遭受“假数学”的流行——强调公式和步骤的死记硬背，而不是理解数学如何影响我们看待世界的方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: Andrew Hacker, for the record, remains skeptical.
paragraphs.translationZh: 据记录，安德鲁·哈克仍然持怀疑态度。

paragraphs.sourceText: “I'm going to leave it to those who are in mathematics to work out the ways to make their subject interesting and exciting so students want to take it,” Hacker says. “All that I ask is that alternatives be offered instead of putting all of us on the road to calculus.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “我将把这个任务留给那些数学专业的人来想办法让他们的学科变得有趣和令人兴奋，这样学生们就愿意接受它，”哈克说。 “我所要求的只是提供替代方案，而不是让我们所有人走上微积分之路。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 51 至 55 题基于以下段落

paragraphs.sourceText: For years, the U.S. has experienced a shortage of registered nurses. The Bureau of Labor Statistics projects that while the number of nurses will increase by 19 percent by 2022, demand will grow faster than supply, and that there will be over one million unfilled nursing jobs by then.
paragraphs.translationZh: 多年来，美国一直面临注册护士短缺的问题。美国劳工统计局预计，虽然到 2022 年护士人数将增加 19%，但需求增长速度将快于供给增长，届时将有超过 100 万个护理岗位空缺。

paragraphs.sourceText: So what's the solution? Robots.
paragraphs.translationZh: 那么解决办法是什么呢？机器人。

paragraphs.sourceText: Japan is ahead of the curve when it comes to this trend. Toyohashi University of Technology has developed Terapio, a robotic medical cart that can make hospital rounds, deliver medications and other items, and retrieve records. It follows a specific individual, such as a doctor or nurse, who can use it to record and access patient data. This type of robot will likely be one of the first to be implemented in hospitals because it has fairly minimal patient contact.
paragraphs.translationZh: 日本在这一趋势方面处于领先地位。丰桥工业大学开发了 Terapio，这是一种机器人医疗车，可以进行医院查房、运送药物和其他物品以及检索记录。它跟随特定的个人，例如医生或护士，可以使用它来记录和访问患者数据。这种类型的机器人可能是最先在医院应用的机器人之一，因为它与患者的接触相当少。

paragraphs.sourceText: Robots capable of social engagement help with loneliness as well as cognitive functioning, but the robot itself doesn't have to engage directly—it can serve as an intermediary for human communication. Telepresence robots such as MantaroBot, Vgo, and Giraff can be controlled through a computer, smartphone, or tablet, allowing family members or doctors to remotely monitor patients or Skype them, often via a screen where the robot's ‘face’ would be. If you can't get to the nursing home to visit grandma, you can use a telepresence robot to hang out with her. A 2016 study found that users had a “consistently positive attitude” about the Giraff robot's ability to enhance communication and decrease feelings of loneliness.
paragraphs.translationZh: 具有社交参与能力的机器人有助于缓解孤独感和认知功能，但机器人本身不必直接参与——它可以充当人类交流的中介。 MantaroBot、Vgo 和 Giraff 等远程呈现机器人可以通过计算机、智能手机或平板电脑进行控制，允许家庭成员或医生远程监控患者或通过 Skype 与他们联系，通常是通过机器人“脸”所在的屏幕。如果你不能去养老院看望奶奶，你可以使用远程呈现机器人和她一起出去玩。 2016 年的一项研究发现，用户对 Giraff 机器人增强沟通和减少孤独感的能力抱有“一贯的积极态度”。

paragraphs.sourceText: A robot's appearance affects its ability to successfully interact with humans, which is why the RIKEN-TRI Collaboration Center for Human-Interactive Robot Research decided to develop a robotic nurse that looks like a huge teddy bear. RIBA (Robot for Interactive Body
paragraphs.translationZh: 机器人的外观影响其与人类成功互动的能力，这就是为什么 RIKEN-TRI 人机交互机器人研究合作中心决定开发一款看起来像巨大泰迪熊的机器人护士。 RIBA（互动身体机器人

paragraphs.sourceText: On the less cute and more scary side there is Actroid F, which is so human-like that some patients may not know the difference. This conversational robot companion has cameras in its eyes, which allow it to track patients and use appropriate facial expressions and body language in its interactions. During a month-long hospital trial, researchers asked 70 patients how they felt being around the robot and “only three or four said they didn't like having it around.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 不太可爱、更可怕的一面是 Actroid F，它非常像人类，以至于一些患者可能不知道其中的区别。这个对话机器人伴侣的眼睛里有摄像头，这使得它能够跟踪患者并在互动中使用适当的面部表情和肢体语言。在为期一个月的医院试验中，研究人员询问了 70 名患者在机器人周围的感受，“只有三到四人表示他们不喜欢机器人在身边。”

paragraphs.sourceText: It's important to note that robotic nurses don't decide courses of treatment or make diagnoses (though robot doctors and surgeons may not be far off). Instead, they perform routine and laborious tasks, freeing nurses up to attend to patients with immediate needs. This is one industry where it seems the integration of robots will lead to collaboration, not replacement.
paragraphs.translationZh: 值得注意的是，机器人护士不会决定治疗方案或进行诊断（尽管机器人医生和外科医生可能离我们并不遥远）。相反，他们执行日常和繁重的任务，使护士能够腾出时间来照顾有紧急需要的患者。在这一行业中，机器人的集成似乎将带来协作，而不是替代。
